title: Text and Streams
summary: A string stores text. A stream moves data into or out of a program. Think of a stream as a small pipe that carries words and numbers.
introduction: A string stores text. A stream moves data into or out of a program. Think of a stream as a small pipe that carries words and numbers. Read one example at a time. Save it in a .cpp file and use the compiler from the setup lesson to run it.
learningObjectives: Read a name and number from text
Build a message with a text stream

blocks.text: std::string holds text. The plus sign joins strings. size() gives the number of char values; that is the letter count for these simple English letters.

blocks.title: strings-streams.cpp

blocks.text: istringstream reads values from text. The >> operator reads one value at a time. Spaces divide the values here.

blocks.title: strings-streams.cpp

blocks.text: ostringstream builds text using <<. Its str() function gives you the finished string.

blocks.title: strings-streams.cpp
Watch out
blocks.text: Check that reading succeeded before using the value. Text such as "five" cannot be read into an int with >>.

blocks.text: Change the note to Ravi 7. Predict the new message.
